title: My first game: AI agents wrote the code from specs I wrote first. I'd love your honest critique
author: Massive-State2698
selftext:
Hi everyone. Melbees: The Secret of Bees is my first game, and it's now out on Google Play and the Microsoft Store. I'm posting it here because of how it was made: I wrote the rules as specs, and AI coding agents wrote the code from them. I'd really like your criticism, of the game and of the process.

The game puts Hangman and Minesweeper together on a honeycomb. On each hex you match or discard the letter. The Pollen number counts the right letters among that hex's neighbours, and a wrong action costs a petal. The picture is a real board from the game, a few moves in, and it doubles as a puzzle: which of the 18 closed hexes are right letters? The numbers force a single answer (checked with a solver), and both words are about stars and galaxies. Spoiler tags for answers, please; I'll post the solution in a comment later. Flowers are letters already matched, and colour doesn't mean right: green letters can only go in word 1, blue in word 2, brown ones are shared.

How the AI part works. Every rule, from the honeycomb to privacy, is written in plain English as a spec before it becomes code, and the specs are the source of truth: when code and spec disagree, the code is wrong. An agent only knows what is written down, so a rule that lives only in my head gets reinvented differently every session. Claude Code writes the code. Before that, each plan goes to agents from other vendors (Gemini and GPT based) for review, because they catch different things. Nothing lands until it passes a local test gate, and nothing ships until I play the release candidate on my own phone.

What surprised me most is how tests can lie. We've had a test runner that silently dropped one file's output and still printed "All tests passed", and a test that went red one day on unchanged code because it signed a token with a fixed date. So a green run gets read, not trusted. The core is a deterministic Dart package (same seed, same board), which gives a Daily Challenge that is the same for everyone and lets the server replay a ranked game from its move log before the time counts. The app is Flutter on Android and Windows, the server is Dart on Cloud Run with Postgres.

Since it's my first game, honest feedback helps most: is the rule clear from the picture, does the first minute make sense, what feels off. As a thank-you, anyone who leaves real feedback in this thread by October 31 gets a year of Premium for free, good or bad feedback alike. It's not a contest, and it has nothing to do with votes or store reviews. To get it, sign in with Google in the game (Settings, Account, Sign in with Google) and send me the account e-mail in a private message. I turn it on by hand, one at a time.

Free download for Android and Windows: https://melbees.games/?s=reddit&c=aigamedev
